narr: A widespread severe weather event impacted Middle Tennessee beginning in the early morning hours of May 8, 2024, and continued through the early morning hours of May 9th. During this time frame, numerous rounds of severe weather moved through the area, causing widespread wind damage in nearly every county in Middle Tennessee, hail up to 3 inches in diameter, and four tornadoes. One of these tornadoes in Columbia prompted a Tornado Emergency to be issued. In addition, major flash flooding also occurred with the worst flooding reported across Robertson and Sumner counties. With nearly nine inches of rain, Flash Flood Emergencies were issued for these counties. This is the first time National Weather Service Nashville issued both a Tornado Emergency and a Flash Flood Emergency in the same event. Unfortunately, this event claimed the lives of five individuals.
ev: Numerous reports of major flash flooding were received across Sumner County, including Gallatin. Impassable roads included Upper Station Creek Road, Liberty Lane, and Long Hollow Pike. Long Hollow Gardens and Long Hollow Golf Course were also reported to be underwater. A house along Long Hollow Gardens was also inundated with flood waters. Life-threatening flash flooding across Sumner County prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for the county. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in southern Overton County, particularly along Highway 164 between Pilgrim Circle and Memory Lane east of Monterey. Damages are unknown.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Putnam County, particularly in Algood where North Allen Road and Dodson Branch Highway were reported to be flooded and impassable. Damages are not known.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Rutherford County, particularly in the Eagleville area and south of Murfreesboro. In Eagleville, Horton Highway at Arno-Allisona Road was reported to be flooded and impassable. In Murfreesboro, Armstrong Valley Road was reported to be impassable. Unfortunately, flooding led to the indirect death of a 10-year-old child who was swept away into a storm drain while playing in the water in the streets.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Lebanon with property flooding reported along Lovers Lane in northeast Lebanon. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding near Sparta with Hickory Valley Road and Lost Creek Road reported to be impassable. Damages are unknown.

Numerous reports of major flooding were received across Davidson County. In Goodlettsville, the Interstate 65 onramp at Long Hollow Pike and Caldwell Drive was flooded. In Antioch, Culbertson Road was underwater while in Hermitage, Stones River Walkway was also underwater. Interstate 24 East after exit 52 was forced to close due to flooding. Damages are a rough estimate.

Numerous reports of major flooding were received across Robertson County, including the Cross Plains area. Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused flash flooding to begin early in the morning on May 8th and continue into the overnight hours. Roads that were reported impassable included Empson Road, Covington Road, and Cross Plains Road. A water rescue had to be performed along Cross Plains Road due to the car becoming submerged in flood waters. Life-threatening flash flooding prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for Robertson County. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain across Marshall County caused flash flooding in the area. Beasley Road in Chapel Hill was closed due to being washed out. Two water rescues had to be performed with one at a residence and the other in a vehicle. Damages are a rough estimate.

Numerous reports of major flooding were received across Robertson County, including the Springfield area. Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused flash flooding to begin early in the morning on May 8th and continue into the overnight hours. Roads that were reported impassable included New Chapal Road and Lahr Road where a water rescue had to be performed due to the car becoming submerged in flood waters. Life-threatening flash flooding prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for Robertson County. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Grundy County. Near Palmer, a section of Barker Cove Road was washed away. Near Beersheba Springs, Highway 56 was flooded and impassable. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding at Dillon Park in Woodbury. Damages are unknown.

Numerous reports of major flooding were received across Robertson County, including the White House area. Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused flash flooding to begin early in the morning on May 8th and continue into the overnight hours. The worst flooding was reported along and south of Highway 76 with specific roadways reported impassable including Sage Road, Melton Road, and Union Road. Flooding was also reported in White House High School. Life-threatening flash flooding prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for Robertson County. Damages are a rough estimate.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received across Montgomery County, especially in the Clarksville area. Several roadways across the county were reported to be flooded and impassable, including Trenton Road. Damages are a rough estimate.

Numerous reports of major flooding were received across Robertson County, including the Greenbrier area. Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused flash flooding to begin early in the morning on May 8th and continue into the overnight hours. One home on Old Greenbrier Pike at Worsham Springs was reported to be surrounded by water. Life-threatening flash flooding prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for Robertson County. Damages are a rough estimate.

Numerous reports of major flash flooding were received across Sumner County, including Hendersonville. Impassable roads included Stop Thirty Road, Drakes Creek Road, Indian Lake Boulevard, Old Shackle Island Road, and Anderson Road. Life-threatening flash flooding across Sumner County prompted the issuance of a Flash Flood Emergency for the county. Damages are a rough estimate.
